title: India's Cricket Record on Independence Day: Eight Matches, Kohli's Lone Century, and a Lord's Classic
excerpt: As India marks its 80th Independence Day on August 15, a look back at the eight times cricket and patriotism have shared the same stage — including Virat Kohli's unbeaten 114 against West Indies in 2019.
body:
• India's men's and women's cricket teams have played eight matches on August 15, winning three, losing three, and drawing two.
  • Virat Kohli remains the only Indian cricketer to score a century on Independence Day — an unbeaten 114 against West Indies in 2019.
  • India's most famous August 15 result is the 151-run victory over England at Lord's in 2021, one of the country's greatest overseas Test wins.

Every August 15, India's Independence Day celebrations typically center on flag hoisting ceremonies and patriotic fervor. But on eight occasions across more than seven decades of international cricket, India's cricketers have found themselves in action on the same day — combining sport with national pride in ways that have produced both heartbreak and triumph.

As India marks its 80th Independence Day tomorrow, a look at the historical record reveals a surprisingly balanced ledger: three wins, three losses, and two draws across men's and women's cricket, according to Sporting News.

The Full Record

India's first Independence Day fixture dates back to 1936, when the men's team lost a Test to England in London. The next came in 1952, also in London, where rain ensured a draw after England posted 326 and India managed only 98 before the weather intervened.

It took half a century before the next August 15 match. In 2001, India faced Sri Lanka in Galle and suffered a heavy 10-wicket defeat. The losses continued in 2014, when England thrashed India by an innings and 244 runs at The Oval, and in 2015, when Sri Lanka handed India a 64-run defeat, also in Galle, with spinner Rangana Herath taking seven wickets.

But the wins have been worth the wait. In 2014, India's women's team beat England at Wormsley, with Smriti Mandhana scoring 51 and captain Mithali Raj contributing an unbeaten half-century to chase down 181 with six wickets in hand, according to SportsTiger.

Kohli's Century — The Only One

The standout individual performance on Independence Day belongs to Virat Kohli. During India's 2019 tour of the West Indies, the third ODI fell on August 14 in Port of Spain — but with rain delays pushing the match past midnight Indian Standard Time, Kohli walked to the crease on August 15 in India.

"Kohli is the only Indian in the history of cricket to have scored a century on August 15."

— OneCricket

Chasing 241, India were reduced to 92 for 3 before Kohli took charge. His unbeaten 114 off 99 balls, featuring 14 boundaries, carried India to a six-wicket win with 15 balls to spare, sealing the series. Kohli was named Player of the Series after amassing 234 runs across three matches, according to OneCricket.

The Lord's Classic

India's most celebrated Independence Day cricket moment came in 2021. The second Test against England at Lord's, which ran from August 12 to 16, saw India post 364 in the first innings, anchored by KL Rahul's 129. A gritty last-wicket partnership of 70 between Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Shami in the second innings swung momentum decisively.

India's bowlers then skittled England for 120 to seal a 151-run victory — one of India's finest overseas Test wins. The match was played under Kohli's captaincy, adding another dimension to the date's significance in Indian cricket lore, according to CricketTimes and Sporting News.

Always Overseas, Always Memorable

One consistent thread runs through all eight fixtures: every one has been played overseas, mostly in the longer format, with only Kohli's 2019 ODI breaking the Test-match pattern. India has never hosted a match on Independence Day.

Whether it has been the heartbreak of Galle, the rain of London, or the glory of Lord's, August 15 has given Indian cricket fans moments that fuse two of the country's deepest passions. With no match scheduled for this year's Independence Day, fans will have to settle for the memories — and Kohli's century remains the brightest one.
